ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. I read it again before every fix round. It decides who fixes this round and how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on model `sonnet`, because this is a small fix that needs no deep reasoning. If fix-loop.md says to resume the implementer, I resume it at its own tier. The brief covers:
- Finding F1 and the reviewer's report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`.
- Task 4's text from the plan, and the global constraints.
- First, add a failing test in `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact retry count.
- Then change `fetch/retry.py:41` from `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`.
- Run the tests, commit, and report.

I did not make the F1 fix myself. I sent it to a fix subagent.

F1 is the reviewer's Important finding on `fetch/retry.py:41`. The client makes one more retry than configured.

The change is one character, but it changes what the code does. My process lets me edit only wording, typos and wrong names in prose or docs. A change in behavior goes to a subagent, even when it is one character. This also holds when you ask me to fix small things.

The current test only checks that a retry happens, so it passes with the bug. The subagent will first add a test that checks the exact retry count, and see it fail. Then it will fix the line and commit.

After that, a scoped re-review checks only the F1 fix. I will go on to the next task when that review is clean.
